problem_type: Startup repair overwrites another viable installation
symptom: Launching a walkthrough package silently repoints all connected MCP clients away from the installed Nomi.
direct_cause: classifyMcpEntry treats launcher inequality as stale and checks local authentication before installation ownership.
class_root: Automatic configuration repair has no shared distinction between broken resources and a different viable owner.
affected_population: Users with multiple Nomi packages or profiles
JSON and TOML MCP clients including registered profiles
internal_only_reason: The approved internal ownership policy determines when Nomi may rewrite an existing client entry; no third-party runtime change is involved.
invariants: Another viable launcher or profile is never rewritten automatically, even when its credentials differ.
Only a proven broken owned launcher may be automatically repointed; explicit install retains the existing write boundary.
Reading settings never writes host configuration.

door_reduction.why_not: The startup write remains singular. Expanded machine scan includes the existing classifier reads (settings and repair), its state/result type references, shared tuple derivation, and renderer projection. These readers must remain to report disk ownership; none is an additional writer. The retired toast producer and consumer are removed.

generality_proof: Every built-in and registered JSON/TOML entry is classified before the sole startup repair writer. Viability and ownership precede local authentication so other packages and profiles cannot be claimed through another stale category.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Distinguish actual launcher failure from a different viable owner before permitting repair.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The generated door map identifies repairStaleMcpConfigs as its single write call.
clientInfo projects the same classifier without writes for JSON, TOML and custom profiles.
Explicit user action intentionally switches the selected client through writeClientConfig and its isolation guard.

recurrence.reason: Each launch of a different valid package repeats the same host config takeover.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs repairStaleMcpConfigs: appIntegration startup entry
rg launcher-stale / classifyMcpEntry / host-config.repaired across electron, src and tests; traced readMcpInfo, JSON/TOML parser, installMcp and registered profile iteration

prevention.invariant: Launcher inequality is not permission to overwrite a viable owner.
prevention.failure_mode: Different viable launchers return launcher-elsewhere and are excluded from automatic writes.
prevention.strategy: Check owned launcher viability and ownership before local authentication; project the actual target to settings and retain explicit install as the switch action.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove launcher-stale's inequality repair and the transient repair toast producer/consumer; settings shows durable disk state.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Internal classification policy using the existing Node filesystem API.

migration: No eager migration. Retired scripts and proven broken paths still repair at startup; viable other installations change only after an explicit switch.
residual_risks: Executable presence does not certify package signatures or successful MCP handshakes; actual package coexistence and Windows verification must be reported separately.
